\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تعاون} (taʿāwana)}{تعاون (taʿāwana)}]{\ar{تعاون} (taʿāwana) — to cooperate}

\label{lesson:AR-C386-taawana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a council, then the Arabic for a member.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تعاون}}
\textbf{\ar{تعاون}} — \emph{taʿāwana} — \textquotedblleft{}to cooperate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تعاون} \ar{الجيران} \ar{لتنظيف} \ar{الحديقة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taʿāwana al-jīrān li-tanẓīf al-ḥadīqa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The neighbours cooperated to clean the park.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتعاون}, \emph{yataʿāwan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تعاون}} (\emph{taʿāwana}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-w-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to help, to aid\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VI, to help one another: to cooperate.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿāwana}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿāwana}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿāwana al-jīrān li-tanẓīf al-ḥadīqa.} — The neighbours cooperated to clean the park.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a council, then the Arabic for a member, then say \emph{taʿāwana} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تعاون} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To cooperate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تفاوض} (tafāwaḍa)}{تفاوض (tafāwaḍa)}]{\ar{تفاوض} (tafāwaḍa) — to negotiate}

\label{lesson:AR-C386-tafawada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a member, then the Arabic for to cooperate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تفاوض}}
\textbf{\ar{تفاوض}} — \emph{tafāwaḍa} — \textquotedblleft{}to negotiate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تفاوض} \ar{العمال} \ar{مع} \ar{المدير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tafāwaḍa al-ʿummāl maʿa al-mudīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The workers negotiated with the manager.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتفاوض}, \emph{yatafāwaḍ}.

The noun \ar{مفاوضات}, \emph{mufāwaḍāt}, negotiations.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تفاوض}} (\emph{tafāwaḍa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-w-ḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}to entrust; to share\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VI, to consult with one another: to negotiate.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tafāwaḍa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tafāwaḍa al-ʿummāl maʿa al-mudīr.} — The workers negotiated with the manager.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a member, then the Arabic for to cooperate, then say \emph{tafāwaḍa} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صادق} (ṣādaqa)}{صادق (ṣādaqa)}]{\ar{صادق} (ṣādaqa) — to ratify}

\label{lesson:AR-C386-sadaqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to cooperate, then the Arabic for to negotiate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صادق}}
\textbf{\ar{صادق}} — \emph{ṣādaqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to ratify\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{صادق} \ar{البرلمان} \ar{على} \ar{الاتفاق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṣādaqa al-barlamān ʿalā al-ittifāq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Parliament ratified the agreement.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يصادق}, \emph{yuṣādiq}.

It takes \ar{على}: \ar{صادق} \ar{على} …. A friend, \ar{صديق}, is from the same root.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صادق}} (\emph{ṣādaqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-d-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to be truthful\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form III; \emph{ṣādaqa ʿalā} is to confirm a thing as true: to ratify.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣādaqa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣādaqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣādaqa al-barlamān ʿalā al-ittifāq.} — Parliament ratified the agreement.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to cooperate, then the Arabic for to negotiate, then say \emph{ṣādaqa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{صادق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To ratify\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صراع} (ṣirāʿ)}{صراع (ṣirāʿ)}]{\ar{صراع} (ṣirāʿ) — a conflict}

\label{lesson:AR-C386-sira}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to negotiate, then the Arabic for to ratify.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صراع}}
\textbf{\ar{صراع}} — \emph{ṣirāʿ} — \textquotedblleft{}a conflict\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انتهى} \ar{الصراع} \ar{بعد} \ar{سنوات}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{intahā aṣ-ṣirāʿ baʿda sanawāt.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The conflict ended after years.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صراع}} (\emph{ṣirāʿ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-r-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to throw down, to wrestle\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ṣirāʿ} is the Form III verbal noun, wrestling with one another: a struggle, a conflict.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣirāʿ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣirāʿ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intahā aṣ-ṣirāʿ baʿda sanawāt.} — The conflict ended after years.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to negotiate, then the Arabic for to ratify, then say \emph{ṣirāʿ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أزمة} (azma)}{أزمة (azma)}]{\ar{أزمة} (azma) — a crisis}

\label{lesson:AR-C386-azma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to ratify, then the Arabic for a conflict.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أزمة}}
\textbf{\ar{أزمة}} — \emph{azma} — \textquotedblleft{}a crisis\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{مرت} \ar{البلاد} \ar{بأزمة} \ar{صعبة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{marrat al-bilād bi-azma ṣaʿba.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The country went through a hard crisis.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أزمة}} (\emph{azma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʾ-z-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to bite hard; to be severe\textquotedblright{} (Lane). An \emph{azma} is a time of hardship: a crisis.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{azma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{marrat al-bilād bi-azma ṣaʿba.} — The country went through a hard crisis.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to ratify, then the Arabic for a conflict, then say \emph{azma} again
\end{itemize}
